Completion of a bearish chart pattern should take place below the long-term average. Breakdown can breach the average at the same time the pattern completes or a bearish chart pattern can complete in a downtrend already below the average. 

This is how I utilize trend filter. 200 day EMA on daily charts and 40 week EMA on weekly charts.

I will discuss more about these setups >> [link]

There are trend periods and there are consolidations.

Identifying a consolidation period is a must for capturing the following trend period. 

Most of the time the consolidation can be labelled one of the old school classical chart pattern. [link]

Weekends, I go through weekly scale charts and build my shopping list in this time frame. 

More on these >> [link] [link]

Price targets should be used as guidelines only. 

When we identify a classical chart pattern, we are actually identifying a consolidation period. Trends are followed by consolidations and consolidations by trends. 

It is a must to identify the consolidation to be able to participate in the following trend.

Once you capture the breakout signal from a consolidation that the market has recognized, your strategy can turn into a trend following with the help of ATR trailing stops.

Americans have never been this pessimistic about their finances:

A record 41% of US consumers expect their financial situation to be worse over the next 12 months.

This figure has more than tripled since Q2 2024.

By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis, this metric peaked at 23%.

This proportion is also significantly higher than in the 1970s and the 1980s, when CPI inflation was above 10%.

Yes, national debt topped $40 trillion in August—but beware talk of “doom loops” and “death spirals.” Measured correctly, debt is down over the last decade. Down, not up! For example, outside 2020's lockdown-driven GDP dive, US household debt as a percentage of national output has steadily fallen since 2008's financial crisis. I’m not advocating for more debt, but big numbers without context can be misleading.

Worldwide government, corporate and household liabilities in aggregate have also fallen relative to the global economy. Following a spike to 285% in late 2020, global debt-to-GDP ratios unwound all pandemic-era increases to settle back around 246% by the end of last year. The takeaway? Don’t waste your time, emotions or money on headline debt doomerism.
